ranked.headline: Computational methods infer cell-level tissue organization from spatial single-cell data
ranked.summary: Spatial omics methods now pair cell-resolved measurements with bias-aware statistics and alignment tools for comparing tissue architecture across samples.

ranked.headline: Simulation and coarse-grained models map conformational ensembles and binding pathways
ranked.summary: Sampling methods now move beyond static structures to quantify ensembles, pathways, and free energies across mutations, peptides, and binders.

ranked.headline: Probabilistic models now infer genetic and regulatory effects at population scale
ranked.summary: Posterior-based fine-mapping, colocalisation, and pooled reporter designs are now applied at genome-wide and population scales.

ranked.headline: Network-based inference over multi-omic data to rank candidate functions and regulators
ranked.summary: Preprints now extend network inference from paired multi-omic data to regulatory metabolites and microbiome-metabolome shifts.

ranked.headline: Neural models link synaptic, extrasynaptic, and population-level dynamics across scales
ranked.summary: Early-April 2026 items pair connectomes, neural mass bifurcations, and manifold estimators to link structure with multiscale dynamics.

ranked.headline: Computational frameworks for classifying sequence features across genomes and proteins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply long-read, genome-wide, and deep learning methods to editing outcomes, transposable elements, and protein sequence reuse.

ranked.headline: Latent and transport models infer single-cell state trajectories from snapshot data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple generative, optimal transport, and morphodynamic models to reconstruct cell state dynamics from snapshot single-cell measurements.

ranked.headline: Metadata, priors and dynamics encoded into single-cell latent representations
ranked.summary: Structured latent objectives encoding metadata, priors, or dynamics are emerging as alternatives to unconstrained scRNA-seq embeddings.

ranked.headline: Protein language models are mapping bacterial defense and dark protein diversity
ranked.summary: Protein and genomic language models now predict microbial defense and protein function from sequence, packaged as searchable resources for reuse.

ranked.headline: Workflow engineering and AnnData-scale infrastructure target reproducible omics analysis
ranked.summary: Dataset scale now routinely exceeds system memory, making data access the primary training bottleneck, while pipelines are re-engineered for portability.

ranked.headline: Generalizable learned models for biomedical imaging and single-cell data across shifts
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether pretrained and generative models for microscopy, cytometry, and single-cell data transfer under distribution shift.

ranked.headline: Protein language models replace alignment and fixed decoys in proteomics tasks
ranked.summary: Protein language models are now benchmarked against BLAST and fixed decoy strategies in proteomics and enzyme function prediction.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic simulations link cell physics and signaling to spatial tissue organization
ranked.summary: Calibrated and multiscale models now tie subcellular mechanics, cytokine diffusion, and gene regulation to measured spatial cell organization.

ranked.headline: Learned predictors coupled to experimental data and physics-based constraints
ranked.summary: Recent items pair learned predictors for structure, binding and energetics with experimental restraints, curated data and explicit physical terms.

ranked.headline: Faster, portable tools for demultiplexing, QC, bin refinement and fungal ITS abundance
ranked.summary: Long-read and multiplexed sequencing workflows need analysis tools that run at scale and port across environments, which these four preprints address.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-level and pangenome assemblies reveal plant karyotype and trait evolution
ranked.summary: Chromosome-level and haplotype-resolved assemblies now extend to pangenome frameworks spanning Sesamum, buckwheat, Aceraceae and Aurantioideae.

ranked.headline: Docking, MD, and free-energy workflows guide receptor, antibody, and siRNA design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study apply MD, docking, and scoring pipelines to receptor, antibody, and antiviral design targets.

ranked.headline: K-mer methods infer phylogenies, genotypes, and mutation rates from raw reads
ranked.summary: Raw-read k-mer tools now bypass assembly and alignment, with new repeat-robust estimators for mutation rates between related sequences.

ranked.headline: Long-read sequencing resolves haplotype, isoform, and duplication structure
ranked.summary: Long-read assemblies and RNA-seq now resolve diploid haplotypes, pangenome variation, and placental isoform structure at population and tissue scale.

ranked.headline: Host-derived and wastewater reads repurposed for microbial profiling and annotation
ranked.summary: Existing human WGS and wastewater reads are being reused for microbial inference, with depth and placement methods shaping output quality.

ranked.headline: Judging variant and heritability predictors by downstream clinical utility
ranked.summary: New benchmarks score predictors by downstream clinical evidence yield and polygenic risk performance, now including LLM evidence mining.

ranked.headline: Graph networks and residue cliques score protein binding, hotspots and metal sites
ranked.summary: Structure-based scoring tools now target ligand affinity, carbohydrate binding, metal sites and mutational hotspots using graph and clique representations.

ranked.headline: Flow and operator models of biological dynamics across brain, health, and plant data
ranked.summary: Multimodal brain, wearable, and multiome time series now make flow-based and Koopman operator dynamics testable across biological systems.

ranked.headline: Deep models on protein language embeddings target binding, disorder, and peptide design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one published study extend pLM and structure-token models to new endpoints, from mutation effects to peptide design.

ranked.headline: Multimodal fusion for cancer survival: calibration, interaction gains, dynamic prognosis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test whether added modalities improve survival models beyond C-index, probing calibration, interaction structure, and dynamic inputs.

ranked.headline: Generative and foundation models quantify brain aging and stimulation response
ranked.summary: Foundation and generative models now yield intervention-sensitive readouts of brain state and aging, from EEG clocks to predicted stimulation response.

ranked.headline: Predicted structures extend to assemblies and domain-level classification at scale
ranked.summary: Predicted structures now cover proteome-scale domain classes, while new benchmarks test stability, proteomics, and retrieval workflows.

ranked.headline: Deep sequence models predict regulatory activity and cell-type enhancers from DNA
ranked.summary: Reporter assays and single-cell multi-omics now supply direct regulatory measurements against which sequence models can be trained and tested.

ranked.headline: Learned representations supplement sequence comparison for homology and annotation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report embedding-based search, structure-token annotation, and learned alignment filtering across homology workflows.

ranked.headline: Read-level DNA methylation profiling extends to metagenomes, promoters and amplicons
ranked.summary: Nanopore and PacBio reads now support read-level methylation calling across metagenomes, vertebrate promoters and amplicons.

ranked.headline: Sampling and multiobjective ensembles for metabolic model solution spaces
ranked.summary: Flux sampling reviews and Pareto ensemble software now appear alongside multiobjective biomarker selection, all as preprints with preliminary results.

ranked.headline: Deep models of images, sequences and structures map protein and tissue organization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair large spatial and proteome-scale datasets with learned models spanning images, sequences, structures and omics.

ranked.headline: Graph learning and optimal transport for single-cell clustering and integration
ranked.summary: Single-cell methods now integrate multi-modal data at over one million cells while explicitly modeling dropout and graph structure.

ranked.headline: Inferring minority genotypes from bulk, single-cell and cell-free sequencing data
ranked.summary: Treating minority or non-germline genotypes as the inferential target makes reference choice and error modelling central to accuracy.

ranked.headline: Representation and topology choices shape inferred protein conformational organization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that MD feature representation and coarse-grained topology choices alter inferred conformational transitions and large-scale changes.

ranked.headline: Structure-based phylogenies and pangenome graphs resolve viral and primate evolution
ranked.summary: Predicted structures and pangenome graphs now extend genome-level evolutionary inference to deep viral lineages and primate immune genes.

ranked.headline: Statistical models infer unobserved or causal quantities from genotype data
ranked.summary: Reference dependence and robustness are emerging as explicit concerns for genotype-based inference in applied breeding and multi-ancestry settings.

ranked.headline: Computational capsid and genome-in-capsid models built from predicted protein structures
ranked.summary: Predicted coat protein structures now enable capsid-scale and genome-in-capsid modeling of icosahedral viruses such as PCV2.

ranked.headline: Bayesian phylogenetic models jointly infer cell lineages, migration routes, and timing
ranked.summary: Birth-death priors can bias single-cell lineage inference, motivating joint models and explicit diagnostics for prior and model assumptions.

ranked.headline: Computational refinement of peptide identification and spectral library construction
ranked.summary: Tailored in silico libraries and per-PSM modification-combination scoring move proteomics search beyond single delta-mass and generic-model assumptions.
